gaps.sentence: She ___ great pride in her grandchildren's achievements.
gaps.explanation: take pride in something means to be pleased and satisfied with it.

gaps.sentence: It was the manager's job to ___ the bad news to the staff.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the news to somebody
gaps.explanation: break the news to somebody means to tell them something difficult or upsetting first.

gaps.sentence: It was three in the morning, but I was wide ___.
gaps.explanation: wide awake means completely awake; it is the fixed collocation with 'wide'.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ interest on the money it borrows.
gaps.explanation: pay interest is the standard financial collocation.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ sure that all the windows are locked.
gaps.explanation: make sure means to check that something is true or has been done.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.
